body:
Crypto markets showed signs of life on Thursday as the total market cap pushed to $2.24T, up 2.59% in 24 hours, though the rally feels more like a dead cat bounce than genuine momentum. Volume hit $80.3B as traders positioned ahead of what could be a critical technical juncture. The Fear & Greed index ticked up slightly to 12 from yesterday's 9, but we're still deep in extreme fear territory where smart money typically starts accumulating. Despite the green across most majors, this feels like relief buying into oversold conditions rather than a trend reversal.

Bitcoin closed at $63,082, gaining 3.22% on the day and holding above the crucial $62,500 support that's been acting as a floor since the recent selloff. The $29.66B in volume suggests institutional interest remains, but we need to see BTC reclaim $65,000 and hold it for 72 hours before calling this anything more than a bounce. The real test comes at $68,000 resistance where sellers have been waiting. If we break below $62,000, expect a fast move to $58,500 where the next major support cluster sits. BTC dominance at 56.4% shows money isn't flowing into risk-on alts yet.

Ethereum at $1,659.77 gained 2.45% but continues to underperform Bitcoin, highlighting the risk-off sentiment still gripping markets. The ETH/BTC ratio remains under pressure, and until we see that relationship stabilize, altcoins will struggle. Solana led majors with a 3.49% pump to $65.48, while Cardano surprised with a 4.08% move to $0.166. UNI gained 3.64% to $2.53 as DeFi tokens showed some life. However, the weekly numbers tell the real story with ETH down 4.36%, SOL off 3.21%, and ADA bleeding 11.49%, confirming this is still a bear market rally.

Japan's parliament is set to pass sweeping crypto regulation treating digital assets like stocks, which could unlock massive institutional flows from the world's third-largest economy. Meanwhile, BlackRock's income-paying Bitcoin ETF nears launch with fees undercutting rivals, adding more institutional infrastructure. The Philippines central bank called out Binance for operating without proper licenses, showing regulators worldwide aren't backing down despite the recent Gensler departure speculation. US inflation topping 4% is putting pressure on risk assets including Bitcoin and gold, as rate cut hopes continue to fade.

The next 48 hours are critical as we approach weekend thin liquidity. Watch for BTC to either break convincingly above $65,000 or fail and retest $62,000 support. Japan's regulatory clarity could be the catalyst that breaks us out of this range if institutional flows materialize quickly. Key risk remains macro with inflation data keeping the Fed hawkish and any geopolitical flare-ups likely to send crypto lower. The real signal will be whether altcoins can sustain gains if BTC continues higher, or if this remains a Bitcoin-only show indicating continued risk aversion.
